_doc: Edit this file to wire the bot up. Channel and manager handle are the two things that MUST be set before first run. Footers rotate — bot picks one not used in the last 3 posts.

languages._doc: channel_lang = what gets posted to the channel (English for B2B poker B2B reach). preview_lang = what gets shown in your review chat (Russian, faster to skim and decide). Footer is always written in channel_lang — it's part of the actual post.

post_schedule._doc: Day-of-week → post type. Sunday=0, Monday=1, ..., Saturday=6. The 'pitch_post_every_n_days' overrides the day's normal type when N days have passed since last pitch — keeps explicit promo to one per ~10 days. Order is tuned so weekly variety is maximized: case_study (the most engaging) lands midweek when reading attention is highest; checklist on Saturday for slow weekend skims; news_take Friday because that's when industry news typically breaks.

longform_link_pool_doc: URLs of EN blog articles eligible for Sunday longform_link tease. autopost.py picks one at random and passes it to Claude as ARTICLE_URL. Add new articles here when they go live; remove if URL changes. Keep 5+ entries to avoid feeling repetitive across weeks.

footer_variants_doc: Footers are CTAs, not signatures. Each starts with a verb, names a concrete next step, and ends with the manager handle. The bot picks one not used in the last 3 posts so consecutive posts don't repeat.
footer_variants: → DM {manager} to map this for your platform mix
→ Walk through this for your club: {manager}
→ Send your format setup to {manager} — get a deployment plan back same-day
→ {manager} runs ops walkthroughs for clubs in your size band — ping to schedule
→ Want this seeding model for your stakes? {manager}
→ Compare your numbers against operator benchmarks: {manager}
→ {manager}: 30-min call to scope filler density for your format

anti_repeat._doc: How many recent post angle hashes to feed back to Claude as 'do not repeat'. 60 = ~2 months of daily posts.

telegram._doc: channel_id is target for actual posts (e.g. -1001234567890 or @public_channel). review_chat_id is where the preview goes — your personal chat ID or a private group with you in it. Get IDs via @userinfobot or by sending /start to the bot then reading getUpdates.
